learn_ai_points:
- Spotting patterns in many images
- Speed
- Consistency: it doesn't get tired

- Context: the whole person, not one picture
- Patient history and previous scans
- Rare and unusual cases
- Combining tests, like a biopsy
- Talking with patients
learn_line: Not AI versus doctors. AI helping doctors.
about_intro: How the AI in this booth was built, how well it did, and what it cannot do.
about_model_text: The image model is a ResNet18, a common image-recognition network. It started from a model trained on everyday photos and was then trained on breast ultrasound images from the Curated BUSI dataset, each labelled normal, benign or malignant. The images were split into {train} for training, {val} for checking during training and {test} for the final test. The heatmaps use Grad-CAM: they show which parts of the image most influenced the prediction.
about_results_text: On {n} test images the model was right about {accuracy:.0f}% of the time. It caught {caught} of {total} cancers and missed {missed}. It also raised {alarms} false alarms (benign lumps called malignant).
about_small_test: {n} images is a small test set, so these numbers could be quite different on other images.
about_matrix_caption: Confusion matrix on the {n} test images. Rows: the true diagnosis. Columns: the AI's prediction.
about_limits:
- It is an educational demonstration, not a medical device.
- It learned from one public dataset and may do worse on images from other machines or hospitals.
- It sees one image only. Doctors look at the whole patient and confirm with a biopsy.
- It can be confidently wrong, and right for the wrong reason.

public_home_intro: Three ways to explore breast cancer and AI. Can you beat the AI? Look at real breast ultrasound images, make your call, then see what our AI said and where it looked. Tweak the Tumor: move cell measurements and watch a simple model change its mind. Ask AIDA: general questions about signs, risk, myths and where to find help. This is education, not a doctor.

explain_missed: A missed cancer (false negative): the AI said {pred}, {percent:.0f}% sure. Confidence is not truth.
explain_missed_off_target: A missed cancer (false negative): the AI said {pred}, {percent:.0f}% sure, and its heatmap wasn't even on the lump. Confidence is not truth.
explain_missed_on_target: A missed cancer (false negative): the AI said {pred}, {percent:.0f}% sure, even though its heatmap was right on the lump. Looking in the right place isn't the same as getting it right.
explain_false_alarm: A false alarm (false positive): this was not cancer, but the AI said {pred}, {percent:.0f}% sure.
explain_false_alarm_off_target: A false alarm (false positive): this was not cancer, but the AI said {pred}, {percent:.0f}% sure, and its heatmap wasn't even on the lump.
explain_false_alarm_on_target: A false alarm (false positive): this was not cancer, but the AI said {pred}, {percent:.0f}% sure, even though its heatmap was right on the lump. Looking in the right place isn't the same as getting it right.
explain_saw_lump: The AI saw a lump that isn't there: it said {pred}, but this is normal tissue.
explain_mixed: The AI said {pred}, but the truth is {truth}.
explain_right_normal: Normal tissue with no lump, and the AI got it right.
explain_right_on_target: The AI got it right, and its heatmap is on the lump.
explain_right_partly: The AI got it right, but its heatmap only partly covers the lump.
explain_right_wrong_place: Right answer, wrong reason: the AI got it right but was mostly looking somewhere else.
wrong_title: When the AI got it wrong
wrong_intro: The six patient folders from our booth: real mistakes our AI made on test images, and one case it got right, for comparison. This is why a doctor always checks.
wrong_17_text: The AI was over 90% sure this was benign. It was cancer. Its heatmap is a wide band through other tissue and only brushes the tumor's edge.
wrong_25_text: The AI looked in the wrong place: its heatmap is below and to the right of the tumor, almost completely missing it.
wrong_26_text: This time the heatmap is right on the tumor, yet the AI still said benign (56% vs 43%). Looking at the right spot is not the same as understanding it.
wrong_28_text: The lump was not cancer. The AI's hottest area is beside the lump and also covers measurement marks added during the scan. A false alarm means worry, extra tests and maybe an unnecessary biopsy.
wrong_04_text: The AI said malignant and was right, but its heatmap is hottest on a different dark area. An AI that is right for the wrong reason can fail on the next patient.
slide_caption: Illustration: a real benign breast cell sample (FNAC), digitally edited to show what each measurement means. This is not a real patient's change. The AI model doesn't look at this picture; it only uses 5 numbers from the 1993 Wisconsin dataset.
